title: Formal identifier remains stable when warehouse alias is used in UI
gherkin:
Feature: Identifier Alias Consistency
  Scenario: Formal identifier preserved when warehouse alias displayed
    Given a rental item with formal identifier "ITEM-2024-001" and warehouse alias "barcode-12345"
    When the warehouse staff views the item in the UI using the alias "barcode-12345"
    And the staff member saves changes to the item
    Then the backend storage must contain the formal identifier "ITEM-2024-001"
    And the formal identifier must remain unchanged in all downstream operational processes
    And the warehouse alias "barcode-12345" must be preserved as a UI display label only
rationale: The operative context requires that the underlying formal identifier remains stable even when warehouse-facing aliases are used in the UI. This test validates that the system correctly distinguishes between the formal identifier (source of truth) and operational aliases (UI convenience), preventing the divergence documented in conflicts.
usedContextItems: Warehouse-facing identifier may use scanner-friendly or operational terminology as a UI alias, provided the underlying formal identifier remains stable|System must maintain consistent identifier representation across UI, backend storage, and reporting outputs

From: logistics_manager@toolchain.com
Date: 2026-02-22 11:00
Subject: Warehouse handling concern for item identifiers

Hi All,

During the warehouse pilot, the team raised a usability concern around how item identifiers are handled on labels and during scanning.

In daily operations, staff tend to refer to the machine-readable identifier as the barcode or serial code rather than by the formal term used in the specification. The current business-oriented format may be less convenient for the scanning workflow than a more scanner-friendly representation.

For now, please review whether the warehouse-facing identifier should remain just an operational alias in the UI, or whether a separate machine-readable identifier is needed alongside the formal item identifier. The main goal is to reduce ambiguity for staff and avoid slowing down intake and return handling.

Thanks,
Gary (Logistics)

Thanks,
Gary (Logistics)

Gary (Logistics)

Gary (Logistics)

Thanks,
Gary (Logistics)

Thanks,
Gary (Logistics)

Subject: Warehouse handling concern for item identifiers

Hi All,

During the warehouse pilot, the team raised a usability concern around how item identifiers are handled on labels and during scanning.

In daily operations, staff tend to refer to the machine-readable identifier as the barcode or serial code rather than by the formal term used in the specification. The current business-oriented format may be less convenient for the scanning workflow than a more scanner-friendly representation.

For now, please review whether the warehouse-facing identifier should remain just an operational alias in the UI, or whether a separate machine-readable identifier is needed alongside the formal item identifier. The main goal is to reduce ambiguity for staff and avoid slowing down intake and return handling.

Thanks,
Gary (Logistics)
